title: Stratified arrival benchmarking harness for mixed-workload continuous-batching
creator: Marina Chen
description: Create a reproducible load-testing harness that models stratified arrival patterns (steady, bursty, and TTL-driven tails) to measure tokens/sec and p95 latency under continuous batching plus queueing. The goal is to: 1) produce stable, comparable metrics across runs; 2) detect regressions in batching/queueing logic that affect p95; 3) provide artifacts (dashboards, alert rules, and PR CI checks) that developers can run against PRs to validate performance impact.
test_plan: Implement workload generator with three strata: steady (Poisson lambda per second), burst (sudden spike windows), and long-tail TTL clients (sporadic single requests)
Parameterize payload size (token-length distribution), model variant (fp16, int8), and batch timeouts to exercise continuous batching code paths
Collect per-request metadata: arrival_timestamp, queue_enter, queue_exit, batch_size, tokens_generated, seq_length, backend_node_id
Aggregate metrics across runs: tokens/sec (global and per-strata), p50/p95/p99 latency for generation start and completion, batch_size histograms, queue_wait distribution
Run controlled regression experiments vs baseline commit: run 5 seeds per configuration and compute median and confidence intervals for p95 and tokens/sec
Integrate results into Grafana dashboard and add a lightweight GitHub Action that can run a small smoke profile on PRs
Define automatic regression detection rules: 10% increase in p95 or 15% drop in tokens/sec vs baseline with statistical significance at p<0.05 triggers fail-fast advisory
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce three canonical mixed-workload profiles locally and in CI within 10% variance for tokens/sec
p95 and tokens/sec metrics are surfaced on a bench Grafana dashboard with per-run annotations and commit hashes
Regression detector produces human-readable artifact (JSON) that lists offending commits and metric deltas
Documentation and runbook updated with steps to run full experiments and interpret alerts
Small PR smoke-check GH Action added and passing on a demo PR

results_summary: Baseline (commit abc123) - mixed-workload profile A: tokens/sec median 18,200; p95 generation latency 210ms; batch_size median 16

Experiment (PR branch feat/bench/strata-arrivals) - after code changes to batching path: tokens/sec median 17,500 (-3.9%); p95 245ms (+16.7%) indicating a regression in tail latency under burst windows
Bootstrapped variance across 5 seeds: p95 stdev 12ms, tokens/sec stdev 420 tps. Regression was above noise floor for p95 but close to noise floor for tokens/sec
HDR histograms show queue_wait spikes concentrated in nodes with active eviction and KV cache misses, suggesting interaction between cache eviction and batching windows
decisions: Roll back the speculative kernel merge that touched the batch timer while we investigate KV cache interaction (temporary revert PR created)
Add a short smoothing window (50ms EWMA) for p95 reporting in dashboards to avoid noisy alerts for small transient spikes; keep raw values for CI regression checks
Prioritize a follow-up ticket to add per-node tracing and batch coalescing counters to identify hot nodes
Make the GH Action conservative: only smoke-checks on PRs and will not block merges until thresholds are tuned and baseline history exists
